projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The sustained count of 21–25 mobile devices paired with zero camera motion suggests either an unexpected gathering of guests in camera-blind spots or a Wi-Fi presence detection anomaly counting smart home IoT devices rather than people. Verify camera functionality and confirm if guests are expected to rule out a sensor issue or security gap.

The sustained high device count (22–25) paired with zero camera motion and Saturday evening timing strongly indicates a stationary indoor gathering (e.g., family guests or kids' friends) rather than normal household movement. This cross-signal pattern confirms a quiet, localized event and rules out system anomalies or unmonitored activity.

The sustained 20-22 device count paired with zero camera motion since noon indicates a likely stationary gathering (e.g., Miller and Penelope hosting friends) or UniFi presence detection overcounting IoT devices. Verifying this helps distinguish between a social event and a system artifact for accurate automation and security context.

The rebound to ~24 connected devices at 12:12 PM, combined with zero camera activity throughout the entire period, strongly indicates a camera system outage or misconfiguration rather than normal household movement, as a family with children and active dogs would typically trigger motion sensors. This leaves the home unmonitored despite apparent occupancy and warrants immediate verification.

Zero camera activity all Saturday morning combined with presence stabilizing at 19 devices strongly indicates the household is away or in a quiet retreat; the remaining 19 devices are likely stationary IoT equipment rather than active occupants, suggesting it may be appropriate to verify away-mode settings.

Mobile device presence steadily declined from 26 to 19 over 45 minutes without corresponding camera activity, suggesting either a Wi-Fi connectivity issue or family members departing without triggering entry/exit cameras. Worth verifying network status or confirming if anyone left for Saturday activities.

The sustained presence of 24–27 mobile devices combined with zero indoor camera motion at 2 AM strongly indicates a large group of guests is sleeping over or resting quietly throughout the house, confirming a social gathering rather than a security event or device anomaly.

The sustained 24–26 device count with zero indoor camera motion indicates the household and likely guests are gathered in a single area or outdoors (e.g., patio/backyard), which is typical for a Friday night and explains the lack of motion detection.

The sustained 22–25 device count with zero camera motion late on a Friday strongly suggests a large, sedentary guest gathering (e.g., movie or game night) rather than normal circulation; the pattern indicates everyone is settled in a common area, with the count dropping to 24 at 23:09 likely marking the start of the group dispersing to bedrooms.

The sustained 22–25 device count with zero camera motion indicates a stable group gathered in a camera-blind zone, likely keeping the space quiet to avoid detection. This matters because home automation may be incorrectly treating the house as empty, potentially disabling security monitoring or leaving climate/lighting systems in an inefficient state.
